corrected_value.authors: Mazar, N., Amir, O., & Ariely, D.
corrected_value.title: The dishonesty of honest people: A theory of self-concept maintenance

decisions.quote: Multilab direct replication of: Experiment 1 from Mazar, N., Amir, O., & Ariely, D. (2008). The dishonesty of honest people: A theory of self-concept maintenance. Journal of Marketing Research, 45, 633–644. doi:10.1509/jmkr.45.6.633
decisions.reason: Verschuere et al. (2018) is a Registered Replication Report testing a single original study: Experiment 1 of Mazar, Amir, and Ariely (2008, doi:10.1509/jmkr.45.6.633). The shipped original on row 532 (Mazar & Ariely, 2007, 'Temporal Influences on Cheating Behavior: The "What the Hell" Effect', doi:10.1037/e722852011-095) is neither cited nor tested anywhere in the paper; rather, row 532 is a mis-resolved duplicate entry for the replication of Mazar, Amir, and Ariely (2008), as confirmed by row 532's own shipped outcome quote from the abstract describing the replication of Mazar et al. (2008). Following the rule never to remove merely unmatched rows and instead resolve the tested original identity, row 532 maps to blind target 0 (Mazar, Amir, & Ariely, 2008).

decisions.quote: In sum, we did not observe the predicted reduction in cheating following priming with the Ten Commandments. These results call into question the effectiveness of using the Ten Commandments as a moral prime to reduce cheating.
decisions.reason: With the dependent original identity resolved to Mazar, Amir, and Ariely (2008, Experiment 1), the multi-lab direct replication failed to replicate the original finding: across 19 labs in the primary meta-analysis (n = 4,674) as well as all 25 contributing labs (N = 5,786), priming with the Ten Commandments did not reduce cheating compared with the neutral books prime (primary Cohen's d = -0.04, 95% CI [-0.12, 0.04], numerically opposite to the original effect of d = 0.48). Both the shipped coding and the blind coding agree on the outcome 'failed'.

decisions.quote: Mazar et al.’s article is among the most cited in deception research, but their Experiment 1 has not been replicated directly. This Registered Replication Report describes the aggregated result of 25 direct replications (total N = 5,786), all of which followed the same preregistered protocol.
decisions.reason: The paper collects new experimental data from 25 laboratories (total N = 5,786) following a preregistered protocol to directly re-test Experiment 1 of Mazar, Amir, and Ariely (2008). Both shipped and blind codings accurately classify the record type as 'replication'.
